threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for the bus instead of nudging your way in. Locals just seem to merge into the crowd like clockwork.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham and the driver sang along to every song on the radio. Had me chuckling all the way home.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The night I heard a group of kids rapping outside, one of them freestyling about the weeds in the park. It felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg street artists tag not just walls but also bus stops? It's like a gallery for the everyday commute.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows not to trust BART on a Friday evening—those overheated brakes are a telltale sign. Tourists just scramble for an Uber.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy confidently strutting off a packed bus with a full pizza in hand, just before it lurched and sent two people tumbling. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for lounging, but locals actually use them for quick chats and impromptu music sessions. It's a vibe you miss.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look at the TMB map like it’s a treasure map, lost in their own adventure while the locals glide by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newbies by their confused looks when the evening bus doesn't show up. We all know it's just part of the Dalston charm.
Caught a night bus from Brixton and a guy dressed as a dinosaur was having a full debate with a pigeon about the best takeaway. Only in London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the kebab guy on Hermannstraße remembered my usual order, and insisted I try his new spicy sauce. That felt like family.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you catch spontaneous techno parties in public parks, complete with improvised sound systems and eclectic crowds. It’s a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only real locals instinctively know to avoid the Civic Center during a BART meltdown. It’s like a secret survival guide around here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy with a pet iguana on the 38 Geary. It was a perfect encapsulation of the Tenderloin vibe – surreal yet completely normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are just for lounging. Locals know those plazas are for impromptu concerts and daily debates on life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still call it ‘la Sagrada Familia’ instead of just ‘Sagrada’—locals skip the ‘la’ unless they want to flex their Español.
